papers.title: IDO 2019 (official paper)
papers.note: WBPSC test booklet, series SCI/19. Answers and explanations were worked out by Claude because the file had no key. WBPSC did publish a provisional key in January 2020, but it couldn't be found; every answer here has been independently re-checked. 99 of 100 questions are included; Q90 is left out because no option is a clear antonym.

questions.q: What is common to common cold, ringworm, conjunctivitis and whooping cough?
o: No preventive measure is available for any of them
questions.e: All four spread from person to person, so they are contagious.

questions.q: The thyroid gland is situated in our
questions.e: The thyroid sits in the front of the neck.

questions.q: Who is the 'boson' particle named after?
questions.e: Bosons are named after Satyendra Nath Bose (Bose–Einstein statistics).

questions.q: If the length of a rectangle is increased by 20% and the breadth reduced by 20%, the area
questions.e: 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96, so the area falls by 4%. Shortcut: +a% and −a% always gives a decrease of a²/100 %.

questions.q: Which vitamin is called riboflavin?
questions.e: Riboflavin is vitamin B2 (B1 is thiamine, B12 cobalamin).
questions.flag: Option labels reconstructed from a blurred scan.

questions.q: Synonym of ABSOLVE
questions.e: Absolve means to set free from blame, i.e. pardon. 'Accuse' is the opposite.

questions.q: Which of the following is not literature of the Vedic tradition?
questions.e: The Purvas are early Jain scriptures. Vedas and Vedangas are Vedic; Puranas belong to the later Brahmanical tradition.
questions.flag: Answer worked out by Claude; no official key was available.

questions.q: What does GSM stand for?
questions.e: GSM = Global System for Mobile Communications, the 2G cellular standard.

questions.q: P and Q can do a work in 12 days, Q and R in 15 days, R and P in 20 days. In what time will P do it alone?
questions.e: Adding all three pairs gives 2(P+Q+R) = 1/12+1/15+1/20 = 1/5, so P+Q+R = 1/10 per day. P = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30, so 30 days.

questions.q: One horsepower is equal to
questions.e: 1 hp = 746 W (metric horsepower is about 735.5 W, a common trap).

questions.q: The electric bulb was invented by
questions.e: Thomas Edison developed the practical incandescent bulb (1879).

questions.q: How many banks were nationalised in India in 1969?
questions.e: 14 banks were nationalised in July 1969; 6 more in 1980.

questions.q: Choose the word that does not belong to the group.
questions.e: Aver means to assert or affirm. The other three all mean deny or reject.

questions.q: Which award is associated with agriculture?
questions.e: The Borlaug Award (after Norman Borlaug) honours Indian agricultural scientists.

questions.q: The 44th Amendment removed which right from the list of Fundamental Rights?
questions.e: The 44th Amendment (1978) made property a legal right under Article 300A.

questions.q: Fertile black soil, most suitable for cotton, is known as
questions.e: Black cotton soil is called regur.

questions.q: The 'Sepoy Mutiny' (1857) first started in
questions.e: The general revolt began at Meerut on 10 May 1857. Mangal Pandey's earlier act at Barrackpore (29 March 1857) is a known trap.
questions.flag: The official key isn't available, and some books accept Barrackpore.

questions.q: Which of the following is not an alloy of copper?
questions.e: Solder is tin + lead. Bronze (Cu+Sn), brass (Cu+Zn) and gun metal (Cu+Sn+Zn) all contain copper.
The rule is '10' followed by the number, so 12 → 1012.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a commercial crop?
questions.e: Wheat is a food crop; the others are cash crops.

questions.q: Methylated spirit is a mixture of
questions.e: Methylated spirit is ethanol denatured with methanol (a little pyridine may be added).

questions.q: The Khetri project in Rajasthan is famous for
questions.e: Khetri is a copper complex (Hindustan Copper).

questions.q: After a 10% deduction, Rs 45 is still to be paid on an electricity bill. The bill was
Gautam Buddha spread his teachings in the language
questions.e: Pali is the expected answer: the Buddha's teachings are preserved in the Pali canon, and Theravada tradition equates Pali with the 'Magadhi' the Buddha spoke. Modern scholars think he taught in eastern Prakrit dialects (probably Old Magadhi), and NCERT says 'Prakrit, the language of ordinary people', so Magadhi is also defensible.

questions.q: Gasoline is obtained from crude petroleum by
questions.e: Crude oil is separated by boiling range in fractional distillation.

questions.q: Complete: Although adolescent development occurs in an orderly sequence, its timing ___ with regard to onset and duration.
questions.e: 'Although … orderly sequence' sets up a contrast: the timing varies.

questions.q: Which Indus Valley find best indicates commercial and economic development?
questions.e: Seals were used in trade, and Indus seals have been found as far away as Mesopotamia.

questions.q: A mixture of calcium aluminate and calcium silicate is called
questions.e: Portland cement is mainly calcium silicates and aluminates.

questions.q: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 16 and 240. If one number is 48, the other is
questions.e: HCF × LCM = product, so 16 × 240 / 48 = 80.

questions.q: Synonym of ABATE
questions.e: Abate means to lessen or decrease. 'Abase' (to humiliate) is the look-alike trap.

questions.q: The working of the human eye is like that of a
questions.e: Lens → image on retina works like camera lens → sensor.

questions.q: Isobars are lines joining places of equal
questions.e: Iso-bar means equal pressure. Isotherm is temperature; isohyet is rainfall.

questions.q: Which country was India's largest trading partner (as asked in 2019)?
questions.e: The exam was held in December 2019. India's commerce data for FY2018-19 showed the USA ($87.96 bn) just ahead of China ($87.08 bn) as India's largest trading partner, and the USA stayed top in 2019-20. China had been top from 2013-14 to 2017-18, and many prep books still said China, so the setter may have expected China. The ranking changes from year to year (China was top again in 2020-21 and 2023-24; the USA in 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2024-25), so check the latest data.
questions.flag: The answer depends on the year.

questions.q: If p, q, r, s, t are five consecutive odd numbers, their average is
questions.e: The average of an evenly spaced list is the middle term, r = p + 4.
questions.flag: Options partly reconstructed from the scan.

questions.q: Which city is spread over two continents?
questions.e: Istanbul straddles the Bosphorus between Europe and Asia.

questions.q: What is 'mixed farming'?
o: Growing crops and also raising livestock
questions.e: Mixed farming combines crops with livestock. Several crops together is 'mixed cropping', a trap.

questions.q: The first gasoline-powered car engine was developed by
questions.e: Karl Benz's Motorwagen (1885-86) is considered the first petrol car.

questions.q: Complete: ___, shy dogs tend to live much longer than bold, aggressive dogs.
questions.e: It pairs with 'shy' and contrasts with 'bold, aggressive', so docile.

questions.q: Complete: New research suggests that, as threatening as they may feel, ___ relationships can enhance social and emotional development.
questions.e: 'Threatening' plus 'enhance development' fits cross-cultural relationships. 'Harmonious' wouldn't feel threatening.

At what rate of simple interest per annum will a sum double itself in 8 years?
questions.e: Doubling means SI = principal, so R = 100/8 = 12.5%.

questions.q: Kalpakkam in Tamil Nadu is famous for
questions.e: Madras Atomic Power Station and the fast breeder reactor are at Kalpakkam.

questions.q: What did Dmitri Mendeleev formulate?
questions.e: Mendeleev published the periodic table in 1869.

questions.q: The material used in a 'lead' pencil is
questions.e: Pencil 'lead' is graphite mixed with clay. There's no lead in it.

questions.q: Which of the following has not contributed to India's growth?
questions.e: The expected answer is population growth, seen as a drag on per-capita growth.

questions.q: From which part of the plant is turmeric obtained?
questions.e: Turmeric is a rhizome, an underground modified stem.

questions.q: Who was the first Indian Governor-General of free India?
questions.e: C. Rajagopalachari (1948–50). Mountbatten was the first Governor-General but was British.

questions.q: A prescribed set of well-defined instructions for solving a problem is called
questions.e: That is the definition of an algorithm.

questions.q: The rapid increase in fish production is called the
questions.e: Blue = fish; white = milk; yellow = oilseeds; brown = leather/cocoa.

questions.e: μ = c / v, always ≥ 1.

questions.q: The powerhouse of the cell is the
questions.e: Mitochondria make ATP.

questions.q: Synonym of ADAMANT
questions.e: Adamant means refusing to change one's mind, i.e. stubborn.

questions.q: The Rowlatt Act was passed in
questions.e: The Rowlatt Act (March 1919) led to Jallianwala Bagh.

questions.q: Where is the headquarters of the Tea Board located?
questions.e: The Tea Board is headquartered in Kolkata. This is the only West Bengal-industry question in the 2019 paper.

questions.q: Antonym of IMMACULATE
questions.e: Immaculate means spotlessly clean (and, secondarily, free from flaws). The opposite of the main sense is dirty. 'Defective' is the opposite of the secondary sense, so it is arguable, but 'dirty' is the expected answer. 'Spotless' is a synonym trap.
questions.flag: 'Defective' is arguable; no official key was available.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a kharif crop?

questions.e: It passes through 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. Odisha is not one of them.

questions.q: A man walks at 10 km/h and rests 5 min after every km. Time to cover 5 km?
questions.e: Walking takes 30 min. He rests after km 1–4 only (4 × 5 = 20 min), so 50 min.

questions.q: A man swims downstream at 8 km/h and upstream at 2 km/h. The speed of the current is
questions.e: Current = (down − up)/2 = 3.

questions.q: Which state launched 24-hour free power for farmers from 1 January 2018?
questions.e: Telangana. This is a current-affairs question from that year.

questions.q: If the average of a, b, c is M and ab + bc + ca = 0, the average of a², b², c² is
questions.e: a²+b²+c² = (a+b+c)² − 2(ab+bc+ca) = 9M², so the average is 3M².

questions.q: A pendulum clock taken from the Earth to the Moon will
questions.e: T = 2π√(l/g). Lower g means a longer period, so the clock runs slow.

questions.q: Hiuen Tsang visited India during the reign of
questions.e: Hiuen Tsang visited during Harsha's reign (7th century).

insights:
What the 2019 paper actually tested (99 of 100 questions analysed):

  • Arithmetic 20 + reasoning 6 = 26 (the 2026 section has 20). School-level (Class 8–10) work: percentages, profit and loss, time and work, interest, HCF/LCM. The reasoning questions were number series and letter/number coding. Shortcuts matter more than theory.
  • English 9 (10 in the full paper): 3 synonyms, 1 antonym (a second, Q90, is left out), 2 odd-one-out, 3 sentence completions. That's almost all vocabulary, with no grammar questions.
  • Physical science 18 (2026: 15): one-line facts and simple formulas (1 hp = 746 W, μ = c/v, water densest at 4°C, alloys, ores), and 6 'who discovered or invented' questions (Raman, Hertz, Mendeleev, Edison, Benz, Bose).
  • Computers 4: acronyms and basics (GSM, LAN, algorithm, languages).
  • West Bengal industry: just 1 (Tea Board HQ). Environment and energy 2 (Kalpakkam, non-biodegradable nylon). Safety and pollution 0.
  • Old general studies 39: history, geography, biology, polity and economy. These subjects are not in the 2026 syllabus.

What this means for you

  • About 60% of the 2019 paper maps onto 2026 sections, so it's still the best guide to style and difficulty: short, factual, one-step questions.
  • The 2026 pattern gives full sections to safety and pollution (10) and environment and energy (15). It also raises West Bengal industry to 15; that topic was in the 2019 syllabus but drew only 1 question. No past IDO paper tests these in depth, so the WBCS question sets here are the nearest guide. Expect direct facts, names, numbers and dates. That's how the lessons' key-facts tables are built.
  • English needs a vocabulary drill (synonyms, antonyms, one-word substitutions) plus basic grammar (prepositions, voice, sentence correction), as the WBCS English set shows.
  • The 20 mental-ability-and-arithmetic questions need speed: about 20 minutes for the section.
  • Negative marking is only −0.25. If you can rule out even one option, answering is worth it on average. Leave a question blank only when you have no idea at all.
  • Coaching sites (Testbook, PW) report an Unreserved cut-off of 78 for the last cycle (Advt 10/2019, exam 22 Dec 2019). This is not an official WBPSC figure, and it was on the old pattern. Aim for 80+ in mocks.

Questions marked 'Old GS' are kept for reference but left out of the mock-test pool.
